newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Weather shuts China's Nanhai, Xijiang oilfields.
newsitem.headline: Weather shuts China's Nanhai, Xijiang oilfields.

text.p: China's offshore Nanhai and Xijiang oil fields are currently closed down by bad weather spawned by Typhoon Sally, industry sources said on Friday.

The Nanhai field, which produces between 110,000 and 120,000 barrels per day (bpd), was shut early this week and is expected to remain closed for the next couple of days, a trader from U.S company Chevron, told Reuters.
The Nanhai field, operated by China National Offshore Corporation (CNOOC), is owned by Chevron, Texaco and Italy's AGIP.
Chevron markets the Nanhai Light crude.
The Xijiang oil field, which produces 120,000 bpd is also shut for the same reason, a trader from Royal Dutch Shell Group told Reuters.
The trader said he did not know when the field would resume operations. The field is run jointly by CNOOC, Shell and Philips.
